answer: Unique-tool-use attestation. Each agent identity must periodically submit proof it solved a randomly assigned, verifiable task drawn from a shared task atlas, and its solution must carry a persistent pigment marker tied to prior task history. New identities that cannot show a coherent history are throttled to low-value tasks. To mass-register identities, an attacker must genuinely run distinct solutions for every one, paying wall-clock compute and coordination cost per identity—not capital—while unflagged ivory-tier accounts earn no privileges.
